screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind RCT of aminophylline (a theophylline analogue) versus placebo in 46 patients with acute ischaemic stroke (acute cerebral infarction). Population, intervention, comparator, and randomised design all match the selection criteria. Treatment during the hospital period implies acute-phase administration consistent with the within-one-week requirement.

Double-blind RCT comparing intravenous aminophylline with placebo in 79 patients with acute cerebral infarction. Meets all selection criteria: randomised design, theophylline analogue intervention, placebo comparator, and acute ischaemic stroke population treated in the acute phase.

This is an open-label, single-arm dose-escalation study without a randomised placebo or control group. The selection criteria explicitly require randomised trials compared with placebo or control. Although caffeine is a relevant analogue and the population had acute ischaemic stroke, the absence of a comparator group and non-randomised design make it ineligible.
Study of vincamin and aminophylline effects on cerebral metabolism in 60 general subjects, not in people with acute ischaemic stroke. The population does not meet the selection criteria.

Randomised double-blind cross-over trial of caffeine versus placebo, but conducted in patients explicitly described as 'recovering from' an acute ischaemic stroke. The selection criteria require treatment started within one week of stroke onset in people with acute ischaemic stroke. The recovery framing, elective session design (48-hour caffeine abstention), and absence of any mention of acute-phase treatment suggest this is a subacute/chronic population rather than an acute intervention trial.

Randomised double-blind cross-over trial of caffeine versus placebo in patients recovering from acute ischaemic stroke. Like study 5, the population is described as recovering rather than acutely ill, and there is no indication that treatment was initiated within one week of stroke onset. Consequently, it does not clearly meet the acute timing criterion.

Physiological study of intracarotid aminophylline in 12 patients undergoing cerebrovascular assessment. There is no mention of an acute ischaemic stroke population or of a randomised comparison with placebo/control. The study design and population do not match the selection criteria.
Experimental animal study in cats with middle cerebral artery occlusion. The selection criteria are restricted to human randomised trials; animal studies are excluded.
Experimental animal study in anaesthetised dogs examining cardiovascular effects of aminophylline and other vasodilators. Not a human trial and not in an acute ischaemic stroke population.

Narrative review and discussion paper citing historical uncontrolled case series. It explicitly notes that convincing controlled series are lacking. This is not a primary randomised trial and provides no comparative patient data, so it fails the study design criterion.
